full_judgment: 2. The respondents instituted the original suit as plaintiffs for declaration of title to the suit land in the schedule of the plant and subsequently by amendment of the plaint also prayed for recovery of khas possession on alleging that the land measuring 19½ decimals appertaining to mouza-Bagura Alekanda in J.L. No.50 under C.S. Khatian Nos.160 and 178, Plot No.1548 belonged to Gobinda Shil: He executed a will and appointed his wife-Sona Lakhsmi as executrix. Defendant No.3, Ramesh Chandra Shil, was the next reversioner. After the death of Gobinda Chandra Shil, Sona Lakhsmi filed Probate Case No.6 of 1917 before the District Judge, Barisal. Sona Lakhsmi and the reversionar heir leased out the said land to Dinabandhu Gangopadhya (father of defendant Nos.1 and 2) by patta dated 05.11.1941 for legal necessity and delivered possession thereof. In the said patta by mistake Plot No.1549 was written instead of Plot No.1548, but the boundary and the area of the land were correctly written. Since the said pattan, defendant Nos.1 and 2 had been residing on the suit land by constructing dwelling structures thereon on payment of rent, municipal tax etc. The said defendants transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by registered sale deed dated 12.05.1970, but in that sale deed also mistakenly Plot No.1549 was written in lieu of Plot No.1548. During R.S. operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother-Sona Lakhsmi although they had never claimed the same. Husband of defendant No.6 in collusion with Sudhir Chandra Dutta, an employee of defendant No.5, constructed structures on Plot No.804, and as such, the plaint was amended incorporating prayer for recovery of khas possession in respect of 'lcha' scheduled land. The collusively pre-pared wrong record in the name of defendant No.3 and her mother has clouded the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land and hence the suit.
